column1: # *** DOMINGA, FOUND IN A HOUSEHOLD - the 1836 Montevideo census, household 114. ***
# *** The page is headed ANO DE 1836 - DEPARTAMENTO DE MONTEVIDEO. ***

column2: Nacion *** Continente *** ; Estado *** CASADO *** ; Profesion *** HACENDADO. ***
column3: *** The head of the household, and a landowner. *** 'Continente' for a Spaniard or a European - the column distinguishes him from the Montevideo-born.

column2: Nacion *** MONTEVIDEO *** ; Estado *** 'Yd' - idem, CASADA *** ; age *** 28 *** from the index.
column3: *** HIS WIFE. *** She sits second, directly after the male head and before two children carrying his surname, and her status repeats his. *** The census states no relationships at all - this is position and status, and it is as far as the page goes. ***
A daughter of the house, unmarried.
*** A daughter named for her mother *** - which is the naming discipline this archive has watched hold across three generations and two continents.

column1: *** AND THE PAGE SAYS SERENA, NOT LORENA ***
column2: The index files her as *** Dominga LORENA ***; the enumerator wrote *** Dominga SERENA. ***
column3: *** The third spelling discrepancy between this index and its own pages in one day *** - after household 97 and household 229. *** The index is not a transcription of the page; it is a reading of it, and a different one each time. ***

column1: *** IS SHE SANCHO'S DAUGHTER? STILL NOT PROVEN, BUT MUCH MORE THAN A NAME NOW ***
column3: *** FOR: *** Sancho's youngest was *** DOMINGA, 7 in the 1812 padron ***, and this archive has *** never followed her past that page ***. She is Montevideo-born, the right generation, and carries a Lerena spelling. *** A daughter named Dominga fits the family's naming exactly. *** *** AGAINST: *** 28 in 1836 implies *** 1808 ***, and Sancho's Dominga was born about *** 1805 *** - three years out. *** Census ages are what a householder said. *** *** NOT ATTACHED TO SANCHO. *** What would settle it is a marriage act for *** Dominga and Antonio R. Carballo ***, which would name her parents - and that is a far smaller search than the one that found her.

column1: *** A THIRD DAUGHTER, AND SHE WAS BORN IN BRAZIL ***
column2: *** JOSEFA CARBALLO, soltera, born and resident RIO DE JANEIRO ***, married *** MIGUEL CARLOS LEMUS *** (also of Rio de Janeiro, son of Juan C. Lemus and Luisa Acuna) on *** 24 July 1862 at San Francisco de Asis, Ciudad Vieja, Montevideo *** - ark 1:1:X9PN-PYNH. Her parents are given as *** ANTONIO CARBALLO and DOMINGA SERENA. ***
column3: *** THIS IS THE SAME COUPLE, AND IT PUTS THEM IN BRAZIL. *** Lucinda and Dominga were with them in Montevideo in 1836; *** Josefa was born in Rio. *** *** And the FamilySearch Tree attaches this Antonio to 'ANTONIO RODRIGUES DE CARVALHO, b.1803' - so CARBALLO is CARVALHO ***, a Portuguese name, which is what the census column *** 'Continente' *** was saying about him. *** TIER: the Carvalho identification is a TREE attachment, not a document, and is recorded as such. ***

column1: *** AND THEIR OWN MARRIAGE IS NOT IN URUGUAY'S INDEXED RECORDS ***
column2: Searched *** SERENA exact with spouse CARBALLO *** , Uruguay: the only hit is Dominga as *** mother of the bride *** in her daughter's 1862 act. *** Control: the same form, loosened, returns 769. ***
column3: *** SO THE ACT THAT WOULD NAME DOMINGA'S PARENTS IS NOT WHERE THIS ROW EXPECTED IT. *** With a daughter born in Rio de Janeiro, *** the marriage may well be Brazilian *** - or Montevidean and pre-1826, in registers this collection does not index. *** The search was right and the country may be wrong ***, which is worth more than another sweep of the same corpus.

column1: *** CORRECTION: SHE WAS NEVER A CANDIDATE. THIS ARCHIVE PROVED HER ON 14 SEPTEMBER. ***
column2: *** DOMINGA JOSEFA LLERENA FERNANDEZ, born 13 May 1804 at Canelones ***, daughter of Sancho Llerena and Maria Fernandez, *** married CAPITAN DON ANTONIO RUIZ [RODRIGUEZ] DE CARVALLO *** - established from the Catedral act of *** 12 May 1827 ***, which names her outright as *** 'Dona DOMINGA LLERENA DE CARVALLO' ***. Their daughter *** LUCINDA GREGORIA *** was baptised that day.
column3: *** SO EVERYTHING I WROTE ABOUT HER AS AN UNATTACHED CANDIDATE WAS WRONG, AND I ADDED A DUPLICATE PERSON TO THE REGISTER TO PROVE IT. *** 'Dominga SERENA (m. Antonio R. Carballo, 1836 census)' has been removed and its evidence folded into the woman who was already here. *** The Lucinda in the census IS Lucinda Gregoria, baptised 12 May 1827 and nine years old in 1836. *** *** One hour earlier I refused to add three children of household 97 in case they duplicated people already in this register - and then did exactly that here, because I did not look her up first. ***

column1: *** WHAT THE CENSUS AND THE 1862 ACT DO ADD ***
column3: *** The 1836 household itself *** - Antonio entered *** Continente, casado, HACENDADO ***, Dominga at 28, and *** a second daughter also called DOMINGA ***, named for her mother. *** And JOSEFA CARBALLO, born and resident in RIO DE JANEIRO ***, marrying Miguel Carlos Lemus of Rio at San Francisco de Asis on 24 July 1862.
column4: *** So the additions are real even though the identification was not new: a third daughter, a household, an occupation - and BRAZIL. *** Her age of 28 against a baptism of 13 May 1804 is *** four years out ***, which is a census age. *** The Brazil thread stands and is the only genuinely new country in any of this. ***
